text:
sec-oncall: FYI P2 security advisory: plaintext OAuth client secret found in a Grafana dashboard screenshot that was uploaded to a public Confluence page by marketing. The secret grants client_credentials access for the internal analytics app (analytics-service). Immediate actions below.
sec-oncall: Impact: possible token minting for analytics-service integrations. No known misuse yet. Required: 1) Rotate the OAuth client secret 2) Revoke any access tokens issued with that client 3) Remove the screenshot and any cached copies 4) Audit external places where the image may have been copied/published 5) Replace dashboards with secure variable references to Vault.
alice: ack. Which client_id is it? I can rotate and push new secret to Vault.
sec-oncall: client_id=analytics-client-1. Last rotated 2025-11-10. We detected the secret in image file grafana_screenshot_2026-03-22.png on Confluence page "Q1-analytics-overview".
ci-bot: automated scan alert: DLP detected pattern matching OAuth client_secret in image OCR: pattern `[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{40}`. Source: confluence.redwood.internal/spaces/ENG/pages/12345
bob: I'll immediately create a new secret and store in Vault under secret/oauth/analytics-client-1. ETA 10m.
ops: please also revoke all tokens minted by analytics-client-1. I can run the revoke sweep once we have the identifier list.
marketing: OMG — that was an old deck screenshot that slipped into the page. We're removing the page and checking any campaign materials that referenced it. Sorry.
legal: notify if this potentially touched any partner integrations. We may need to send a notice if third parties used tokens from that client.
sec-oncall: good. Checklist for owners: A) Rotate client secret in Auth service: `authctl clients rotate --id analytics-client-1 --store-vault path=secret/oauth/analytics-client-1` B) Revoke tokens: `authctl tokens revoke --client analytics-client-1 --since 2026-03-20T00:00Z` C) Remove image from Confluence and request purge from Confluence CDN: `confluence delete-attachment 12345 grafana_screenshot_2026-03-22.png; cdn-purge confluence/attachments/12345` D) Search for exposures: `rg --hidden "grafana_screenshot_2026-03-22.png" /mnt/cdn /var/www` and `oss-scan --images --ocr "analytics-client-1"`
bob: new secret created and saved. New secret path: secret/oauth/analytics-client-1 (rotated-by=bob, timestamp=1802009990). I'm pushing the new client secret to the auth service now.
ci-bot: note: CI pipelines that reference the old secret via environment variables will fail. Update `ci/analytics` pipeline secret reference to new Vault path.
infra: scheduled token revoke job started. `authctl tokens revoke` returned 12 active tokens revoked for analytics-client-1.
alice: updating code and dashboards to read secret from Vault via secret backend plugin for Grafana. PR inbound: infra/grafana#789.
ops: confirmed revoke sweep completed; all currently active tokens tied to the client have been invalidated. Any long-lived refresh tokens were revoked as well.
marketing: removed the Confluence page and sent a message to the team to check for the image in slide decks and external blog drafts.
legal: please collect a timeline of exposure and who had access to the Confluence page for the incident record.
sec-oncall: forensics ask: pull Confluence audit logs for page attachments and downloads between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-22. Also request CDN access logs for the image object key.
alice: commands I ran: `authctl clients rotate --id analytics-client-1 --out /tmp/new-secret && vault kv put secret/oauth/analytics-client-1 token=@/tmp/new-secret` and `authctl tokens revoke --client analytics-client-1 --since 2026-03-20T00:00Z` (revoked 12 tokens). Grafana PR created to read from Vault.
sec-oncall: containment: secret rotated, tokens revoked, image removed, CDN purge requested, PR for Vault integration in progress. Residual action items: verify any partner systems using analytics-client-1, complete Confluence/CDN purge, add OCR scanning guardrails to DLP to detect embedded credentials in images, and update internal docs to forbid screenshots with secrets.
ops: posting status page draft for internal ops: "Vendor-facing analytics integration secret rotated after exposure in internal Confluence page. No customer data confirmed exposed."
legal: retaining logs and will prepare compliance memo if partner tokens were affected.
marketing: will do an org-wide reminder and training to avoid screenshots with secrets. Also switching to masked images for public pages.
sec-oncall: ETA for full verification: 4h. We'll compile an exec summary after verification. If you find any additional exposures, post here and ping @sec-oncall.
